request.title: Why a Dog's Nose Works in Stereo
request.narration: A dog's nose splits air into two jobs. When a dog sniffs, air does not take one simple path through the nose. It splits. A 2010 study built a computer model of a dog's nasal airway from MRI scans. The simulation showed two separate flows: one for breathing, and one that carries odor molecules to the olfactory region. Each nostril also draws from its own patch of air, because the nose's reach is smaller than the gap between the nostrils. That may help a dog compare scent strength on each side. The nose is a routing system, not just a detector. Its shape helps scent reach the receptors.
